title: Aeroflot 1492
summary: Aeroflot Flight 1492, a Sukhoi Superjet 100 scheduled passenger flight from Moscow Sheremetyevo to Murmansk, was struck by lightning during climb-out at flight level 8,900 meters. The lightning strike caused failure of primary radio and autopilot systems, forcing the aircraft to revert to DIRECT mode flight control. The crew returned to Sheremetyevo for an emergency landing. During approach, the aircraft encountered crosswind conditions and bounced on landing. After bouncing, the aircraft touched down hard, the landing gear collapsed, and fuel spilled from the wings. A post-impact fire erupted in the rear fuselage, killing 41 of 78 occupants. The accident was precipitated by lightning-induced systems failure combined with challenging approach conditions and non-optimal landing technique.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by a combination of factors: (1) Lightning strike at FL89 causing primary radio and autopilot inoperative conditions, resulting in flight control mode degradation to DIRECT mode; (2) Crew attempt to land with excessive crosswind component; (3) Aircraft bounce on landing with subsequent hard touchdown causing landing gear collapse; (4) Fuel system structural damage resulting in fuel spillage from wings; (5) Post-impact fire in rear fuselage section. The investigation determined the crew encountered challenging approach conditions including crosswind and executed landing procedures while aircraft was in degraded DIRECT control mode without standard flight control system protections.

factors.evidence: Aircraft struck by lightning at flight level 8,900 meters at 15:08 UTC. Primary radio and autopilot became inoperative due to electrical failures from lightning strike (p. 15)

Flight control mode degraded from normal to DIRECT mode following lightning strike. DIRECT mode represents degraded, more challenging aircraft operation without normal flight control law protections and automatic trim functions (p. 15-16)
Aircraft bounced on landing, then touched down hard. FDR data and physical evidence confirmed hard landing resulting in landing gear structure failure and fuselage damage (p. 16-17)
Landing gear collapsed under impact forces from hard landing. Aircraft fuselage contacted runway surface during gear collapse sequence (p. 17)
Fuel system structural integrity compromised during hard landing and gear collapse. Fuel spilled from wing fuel tanks following impact (p. 17)

Post-impact fire erupted in rear fuselage section. Fire propagated rapidly due to fuel spillage and aircraft interior materials. Fire caused fatalities and forced evacuation from rear exits (p. 17-18)

Fire in rear section of fuselage prevented evacuation from rear doors. Passengers and crew evacuated primarily from forward doors using slides. 41 of 78 occupants perished, primarily those unable to evacuate from rear sections (p. 18)

events.text: Aeroflot Flight SU-1492 (AFL1492) departed Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport on runway 24C bound for Murmansk. Aircraft carried 2 flight crew, 3 cabin crew, and 73 passengers (78 total occupants). Aircraft configured for scheduled passenger operation.
Six minutes into flight at flight level 8,900 meters (FL89), aircraft was struck by lightning. Lightning strike caused immediate electrical system failures affecting critical aircraft systems.

Following lightning strike: Primary radio systems became inoperative. Autopilot systems became inoperative. Flight control mode automatically reverted to DIRECT mode as a consequence of system failures. DIRECT mode is a degraded control law without normal protections and automatic trim.

Captain assumed manual control of aircraft in DIRECT mode. Transponder code changed to 7700 (emergency). Crew initiated return to Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport for emergency landing due to loss of primary radio and autopilot capabilities.
Aircraft established communications via secondary radio. ATC coordinated emergency descent and approach to Sheremetyevo. Weather conditions reported with crosswind component relative to runway 24L.

Aircraft on final approach to runway 24L in DIRECT control mode. Crew configured aircraft for landing with flaps at 25 degrees in preparation for overweight landing. Crosswind component present but crew did not initiate go-around.

Aircraft bounced on landing. After bounce, aircraft touched down hard at runway surface. Landing gear shock struts exceeded design load limits. Fuselage contacted runway surface during landing sequence.

Landing gear structural failure and collapse. Main landing gear legs separated from fuselage. Fuel system structural damage sustained during hard impact and gear collapse. Fuel spilled rapidly from wing fuel tanks. Post-impact fire erupted in rear fuselage section, propagated by fuel and interior materials. Fire rapidly consumed rear section of aircraft, preventing evacuation from rear doors. Passengers and crew evacuated from forward doors using emergency slides. 41 of 78 occupants died; majority from fire exposure or evacuation barrier created by fire.

recommendations.text: Develop and implement enhanced crew training procedures for emergency operations in degraded flight control modes including DIRECT mode

recommendations.recipient: Sukhoi Civil Aircraft and aircraft manufacturers
recommendations.text: Review and enhance lightning strike protection systems for critical avionics and flight control computers
Implement procedures ensuring crew executes go-around when crosswind limits are approached or exceeded during approach
Enhance emergency evacuation procedures and training for incidents involving post-impact fire in rear fuselage sections
Review structural integrity of landing gear attachment points and fuel system components to withstand hard landing scenarios
Establish mandatory go-around procedures when aircraft control systems are degraded and approach conditions are marginal
Review redundancy of primary flight control systems to reduce likelihood of complete mode reversion to DIRECT control
Enhance weather reporting and crosswind forecasting for Moscow Sheremetyevo operations
